name: Brazil
blurb: Bigger than the contiguous United States, and home to 60% of the Amazon rainforest.

name: Mexico
blurb: Chocolate, chillies, and vanilla were all first domesticated here.

name: Argentina
blurb: Its name comes from argentum, Latin for silver — a metal early explorers never found there.

name: Chile
blurb: Over 4,300 km long but on average just 180 km wide, squeezed between the Andes and the Pacific.

name: Colombia
blurb: The only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific and the Caribbean.

name: Peru
blurb: Potatoes were first domesticated here — Peru still grows over 4,000 varieties.

name: Venezuela
blurb: Angel Falls drops 979 m here, nearly twenty times the height of Niagara.

name: Bolivia
blurb: One of only two landlocked countries in the Americas, with a navy that patrols Lake Titicaca.

name: Ecuador
blurb: Named after the equator, it also owns the Galápagos Islands 1,000 km offshore.

name: Panama
blurb: Ships crossing its famous canal are lifted 26 m above sea level by giant locks.

name: Costa Rica
blurb: It abolished its army in 1948 and spent the money on schools instead.

name: France
blurb: Thanks to overseas territories, it spans more time zones than any other country: twelve.

name: Italy
blurb: Two independent countries sit entirely inside it: San Marino and Vatican City.

name: Spain
blurb: Spaniards eat twelve grapes at midnight on New Year's Eve, one for each chime.

name: Germany
blurb: A third of the country is still forest, including the fairy-tale Black Forest.

name: Portugal
blurb: Its borders have barely moved since 1297 — among the oldest in Europe.

name: Netherlands
blurb: About a third of the country sits below sea level, held back by dikes and pumps.

name: Poland
blurb: Europe's last primeval lowland forest, Białowieża, still shelters wild bison here.

name: Russia
blurb: It spans 11 time zones — the train from Moscow to Vladivostok takes a full week.

name: Iceland
blurb: Volcanoes and hot springs heat almost every home in the country.

name: Finland
blurb: Roughly 188,000 lakes — and about one sauna for every two Finns.

name: Austria
blurb: This Alpine republic gave the world Mozart, Freud, and the croissant's ancestor, the kipferl.

name: Romania
blurb: Bran Castle in Transylvania fuels the Dracula legend, though Vlad barely stayed there.

name: Czechia
blurb: Czechs drink more beer per person than any other nation on Earth.

name: Egypt
blurb: Around 95% of Egyptians live on just 5% of the land, hugging the Nile.

name: South Africa
blurb: It has three capital cities — Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein.

name: Nigeria
blurb: One in six Africans is Nigerian, and its film industry out-produces Hollywood.

name: Kenya
blurb: The Great Rift Valley slices right through it, and the equator crosses Mount Kenya's slopes.

name: Morocco
blurb: Only 14 km of the Strait of Gibraltar separate it from Europe.

name: Ethiopia
blurb: Never colonised, it follows its own calendar — about seven years behind everyone else's.

name: Algeria
blurb: Africa's largest country, with the Sahara covering more than four-fifths of it.

name: Madagascar
blurb: Cut off for 88 million years, so most of its wildlife — lemurs included — exists nowhere else.

name: Tanzania
blurb: Africa's highest peak, Kilimanjaro, rises here just south of the Kenyan border.

name: Libya
blurb: A spot here once claimed the hottest temperature ever recorded: 58°C in 1922.

name: Sudan
blurb: It has more pyramids than Egypt — over 200, built by the Kingdom of Kush.

name: Ghana
blurb: Lake Volta, formed by a dam here, is the world's largest reservoir by surface area.

name: Somalia
blurb: Its coastline is the longest in mainland Africa, wrapping around the Horn.

name: Zimbabwe
blurb: Named for Great Zimbabwe, a medieval stone city whose walls stand without mortar.

name: Tunisia
blurb: Star Wars filmed Tatooine here — in a real town called Tataouine.

name: India
blurb: A billion-plus people, 22 official languages, and the world's largest film industry.

name: China
blurb: All of the Great Wall's branches laid end to end would stretch over 21,000 km.

name: Indonesia
blurb: Spread across 17,000-plus islands, it's the world's largest archipelago nation.

name: Thailand
blurb: Never colonised by a European power — the only Southeast Asian nation that can say so.

name: Philippines
blurb: More than 7,600 islands, only about 2,000 of them inhabited.

name: Malaysia
blurb: Split in two by the South China Sea, with half the country on the island of Borneo.

name: Saudi Arabia
blurb: Its Empty Quarter is the largest continuous sand desert on Earth.

name: Iran
blurb: Ancient qanat tunnels have carried mountain water to its desert towns for 2,700 years.

name: Iraq
blurb: Writing, the wheel, and beer brewing all trace back to ancient Mesopotamia, here.

name: Afghanistan
blurb: Lapis lazuli for Tutankhamun's death mask was mined in its mountains.

name: Mongolia
blurb: The world's least densely populated country — horses outnumber people.

name: Kazakhstan
blurb: The world's largest landlocked country, and where every Soviet cosmonaut launched from.

name: Sri Lanka
blurb: Once called Ceylon, it still ships more tea than almost anyone else.

name: Australia
blurb: Its Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth, visible from space.

name: New Zealand
blurb: One of the last major lands humans settled — Māori arrived only about 750 years ago.

name: Papua New Guinea
blurb: Over 800 languages are spoken here — more than anywhere else on Earth.

name: Japan
blurb: The hinomaru's red disc has represented the rising sun for over a millennium.

name: Canada
blurb: The maple leaf design was only adopted in 1965, after a heated national debate.

name: United States
blurb: Fifty stars, one per state; thirteen stripes for the original colonies.

name: United Kingdom
blurb: The Union Jack overlays the crosses of England, Scotland, and Ireland.

name: Switzerland
blurb: One of only two square national flags — the other belongs to Vatican City.

name: Greece
blurb: Nine stripes, said to match the syllables of the Greek war cry for freedom.

name: Jamaica
blurb: The only national flag with none of the colours red, white, or blue.

name: South Korea
blurb: The circle is a yin-yang; the black trigrams around it come from the I Ching.

name: Israel
blurb: Its blue stripes echo the tallit, the traditional Jewish prayer shawl.

name: Turkey
blurb: Star and crescent on red — a design inherited from the Ottoman Empire.

name: Nepal
blurb: The only national flag that isn't a rectangle: two stacked pennants.

name: Denmark
blurb: The Dannebrog is the oldest national flag still in use, dating to the 1200s.

name: Sweden
blurb: A yellow Nordic cross on blue, colours borrowed from the royal coat of arms.

name: Norway
blurb: Hidden inside its cross are the flags of six other countries, including France.

name: Cuba
blurb: The lone star stands for independence; exiles designed it in New York in 1849.

name: Ireland
blurb: Green for Catholics, orange for Protestants, white for the peace between them.

name: Ukraine
blurb: Blue over yellow: a clear sky above a ripe wheat field.

name: Vietnam
blurb: A gold star on red, flown in Hanoi since independence was declared in 1945.

name: Pakistan
blurb: The white stripe was added to represent the country's non-Muslim minorities.

name: Bangladesh
blurb: Its red disc sits slightly off-centre so it looks centred when flying.

name: Paris
blurb: The Eiffel Tower was meant to be torn down after twenty years.

name: London
blurb: Big Ben is the bell, not the tower it hangs in.

name: Rome
blurb: Coins tossed in the Trevi Fountain — about 1.5 million euros a year — go to charity.

name: Madrid
blurb: Western Europe's highest major capital, sitting on a plateau at about 650 m.

name: Berlin
blurb: It has more bridges than Venice — around 1,700 of them.

name: Lisbon
blurb: Rebuilt on a grid after a catastrophic earthquake and tsunami in 1755.

name: Vienna
blurb: Regularly voted the world's most liveable city; Beethoven and Mozart both worked here.

name: Athens
blurb: Continuously inhabited for over 3,400 years, with democracy invented up the hill.

name: Amsterdam
blurb: Built on millions of wooden piles, with more canals than Venice.

name: Warsaw
blurb: Flattened in WWII, its Old Town was rebuilt brick by brick from old paintings.

name: Prague
blurb: Its medieval astronomical clock has been ticking since 1410.

name: Budapest
blurb: Two cities, Buda and Pest, merged across the Danube in 1873.

name: Dublin
blurb: The Guinness brewery here signed a 9,000-year lease in 1759.

name: Stockholm
blurb: Spread across 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.

name: Oslo
blurb: Winners collect the Nobel Peace Prize here, not in Stockholm.

name: Bern
blurb: Switzerland's capital isn't Zurich or Geneva — it's this medieval town on the Aare.

name: Moscow
blurb: Its metro stations are palaces of marble, mosaics, and chandeliers.

name: Kyiv
blurb: Founded around the 5th century, it's older than Moscow by some 600 years.

name: Cairo
blurb: The last surviving ancient wonder, the Great Pyramid, stands on its western edge.

name: Nairobi
blurb: The only capital with a national park — lions live within sight of skyscrapers.

name: Rabat
blurb: Morocco's capital isn't Casablanca or Marrakesh — it's this quieter Atlantic city.

name: Addis Ababa
blurb: Africa's diplomatic capital, hosting the African Union at 2,355 m altitude.

name: Accra
blurb: Its name comes from an Akan word for soldier ants.

name: Dakar
blurb: Mainland Africa's westernmost city, out on the Cap-Vert peninsula.

name: Kampala
blurb: Said to be built, like Rome, on seven hills — near the shore of Lake Victoria.

name: Algiers
blurb: Whitewashed buildings cascading to the bay earned it the name 'Algiers the White'.

name: Tunis
blurb: The ruins of ancient Carthage sit in its northern suburbs.

name: Abuja
blurb: A planned city that replaced coastal Lagos as Nigeria's capital in 1991.

name: Kinshasa
blurb: The world's largest French-speaking city — bigger than Paris.

name: Antananarivo
blurb: Its name means 'city of the thousand', for the soldiers who once guarded it.

name: Harare
blurb: Sitting on a plateau at 1,500 m, this tropical capital stays surprisingly mild.

name: Pretoria
blurb: South Africa's executive capital, purple with jacaranda blooms every October.

name: Tokyo
blurb: The world's biggest metropolis — greater Tokyo holds around 37 million people.

name: Beijing
blurb: Its Forbidden City has 8,700-plus rooms and housed 24 emperors.

name: Seoul
blurb: Half of all South Koreans live in its metropolitan area.

name: Bangkok
blurb: Its full ceremonial name runs 168 letters — a world record for a place name.

name: Hanoi
blurb: A thousand-year-old capital where motorbikes outnumber cars ten to one.

name: Jakarta
blurb: Sinking so fast that Indonesia is building a replacement capital on Borneo.

name: Manila
blurb: Its walled core, Intramuros, anchored Spain's Pacific empire for 300 years.

name: Kuala Lumpur
blurb: Its Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings at the millennium.

name: New Delhi
blurb: A British-built district inside Delhi, a city ruled by seven earlier empires.

name: Islamabad
blurb: Purpose-built in the 1960s in the Himalayan foothills to replace Karachi.

name: Kathmandu
blurb: Gateway to Everest, ringed by Himalayan peaks and centuries-old pagodas.

name: Riyadh
blurb: A mud-walled desert town a century ago, now a metropolis of eight million.

name: Tehran
blurb: The snow-capped Alborz mountains rise directly behind its skyline.

name: Baghdad
blurb: In the 9th century its House of Wisdom made it the largest city on Earth.

name: Amman
blurb: Built over the ancient city of Philadelphia — its Roman theatre still hosts shows.

name: Ankara
blurb: Atatürk moved the capital here from Istanbul in 1923 for its safe central location.

name: Astana
blurb: One of the world's coldest capitals, with winters plunging past minus 35°C.

name: Ulaanbaatar
blurb: The coldest capital city on Earth, averaging below freezing across the year.

name: Dhaka
blurb: The rickshaw capital of the world, with hundreds of thousands on its streets.

name: Singapore
blurb: A city, an island, and a country all at once — one of the last true city-states.

name: Ottawa
blurb: Its Rideau Canal becomes the world's largest skating rink every winter.

name: Washington, D.C.
blurb: A diamond of land carved out in 1790 purely to house the US government.

name: Mexico City
blurb: Built on a drained Aztec lake, it's sinking up to 50 cm every year.

name: Havana
blurb: Classic 1950s American cars still cruise its Malecón seafront.

name: Kingston
blurb: Reggae's birthplace, beside the world's seventh-largest natural harbour.

name: Lima
blurb: One of the driest capitals on Earth, yet it sits right beside the Pacific.

name: Bogotá
blurb: Perched in the Andes at 2,640 m — one of the highest capitals in the world.

name: Santiago
blurb: On clear days the snow-capped Andes tower directly over its skyline.

name: Buenos Aires
blurb: Birthplace of tango, with an opera house rated among the world's finest.

name: Brasília
blurb: Built from scratch in just 41 months and inaugurated as capital in 1960.

name: Quito
blurb: The closest capital to the equator — the line passes just north of town.

name: Montevideo
blurb: Over a third of all Uruguayans live here, on the Río de la Plata.

name: Caracas
blurb: A cable car climbs from its valley to the 2,100 m Ávila ridge above.

name: Canberra
blurb: A compromise capital, purpose-built because Sydney and Melbourne both wanted the job.

name: Wellington
blurb: The world's southernmost capital, famously windy on the Cook Strait.

name: Barcelona
blurb: The Sagrada Família has been under construction since 1882.

name: Istanbul
blurb: The only major city that straddles two continents, Europe and Asia.

name: Rio de Janeiro
blurb: Christ the Redeemer watches from 700 m above the city's beaches.

name: São Paulo
blurb: The Southern Hemisphere's largest city, with more Japanese roots than anywhere outside Japan.

name: Mumbai
blurb: Seven islands merged by land reclamation, and now the home of Bollywood.

name: Shanghai
blurb: Its maglev train hits 431 km/h on the short run in from the airport.

name: Sydney
blurb: Its Opera House roof is covered in more than a million tiles.

name: Melbourne
blurb: It served as Australia's capital for 26 years while Canberra was being built.

name: Casablanca
blurb: Morocco's biggest city, where a 210 m mosque minaret towers over the Atlantic.

name: Vancouver
blurb: Ski slopes and ocean beaches sit within half an hour of downtown.

name: Toronto
blurb: Over half its residents were born outside Canada — among the world's most diverse cities.

name: Cape Town
blurb: Flat-topped Table Mountain rises a full kilometre straight out of the city.

name: Chicago
blurb: Engineers reversed its river's flow in 1900 to protect Lake Michigan.

name: New York City
blurb: More than 800 languages are spoken here — the most of any city on Earth.

name: Los Angeles
blurb: Its original Spanish name ran over 40 letters; Hollywood came much later.

name: Dubai
blurb: From the Burj Khalifa's top floors you can watch the sunset twice in one evening.

name: St Petersburg
blurb: Russia's imperial capital for two centuries, raised on a swamp by Peter the Great.

name: Munich
blurb: Its Oktoberfest actually starts in September.

name: Milan
blurb: Its Gothic cathedral took nearly six centuries to finish.

name: Venice
blurb: Its 118 lagoon islands are laced together by more than 400 bridges.

name: Kyoto
blurb: Japan's capital for over 1,000 years, with some 1,600 Buddhist temples.

name: Karachi
blurb: Pakistan's port megacity of 17 million began as a small fishing village.

name: Lagos
blurb: Africa's largest metropolis, adding an estimated 3,000 new residents a day.

name: Alexandria
blurb: Founded by Alexander the Great, it held the ancient world's greatest library.

name: Mecca
blurb: Islam's holiest city, which non-Muslims are not permitted to enter.

name: Auckland
blurb: Built across a field of about 50 volcanoes, with more boats per person than anywhere.

name: Medellín
blurb: Once notorious, now feted for its cable cars and 'eternal spring' climate.

name: Ho Chi Minh City
blurb: Still called Saigon by many locals, it's Vietnam's largest city.

name: Geneva
blurb: Headquarters of the Red Cross and CERN, wrapped on three sides by France.

name: Cusco
blurb: Capital of the Inca Empire, and the gateway to Machu Picchu.

name: Portugal
blurb: The armillary sphere on it honours the navigators of the Age of Discovery.

name: South Africa
blurb: Six colours and a sideways Y, designed in a single week for the 1994 elections.

name: Mexico
blurb: The eagle eating a snake on a cactus marks where the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan.

name: Kenya
blurb: A Maasai shield and crossed spears guard the black, red, and green.

name: Uruguay
blurb: Its Sun of May and stripes are easy to mistake for neighbouring Argentina's.

name: Argentina
blurb: The golden Sun of May commemorates the 1810 revolution against Spain.

name: Colombia
blurb: Yellow takes the whole top half — unlike near-twins Venezuela and Ecuador.

name: Indonesia
blurb: Red over white — flip it and you have Poland; shrink it and it's Monaco.

name: Thailand
blurb: Red, white, and blue stripes — the central blue band honoured its WWI allies.

name: Philippines
blurb: Flown with red on top instead of blue, it signals the country is at war.

name: Ghana
blurb: First flag to pair the pan-African red, gold, and green with a black star.

name: Malaysia
blurb: Stripes and a canton like the US flag, but with a crescent and 14-point star.

name: Chile
blurb: One star and red-white-blue — often confused with the Texas Lone Star flag.

name: New Zealand
blurb: Its red Southern Cross stars set it apart from Australia's all-white ones.

name: Egypt
blurb: The golden Eagle of Saladin perches on the middle white band.
